clue.text: Wood, possibly, and where it may be used

definitions.meaning: a wood is one kind of stick used to hit the ball on the links
the members' association and premises where the game is played

explanation.surface: A riddle about a piece of timber and the place it gets put to use.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a stick such as a wood and the society or course where golfers play, a double sense.

clue.text: Vassal rejects lie about monarch being foreign

indicators.note: the shortened vassal goes round the royal letter
the vassal throws out the word lie from his title

parts.note: a liegeman is a feudal vassal sworn to a lord
taken as written
R, for rex or regina, is the usual abbreviation for a monarch

explanation.surface: A feudal underling refuses to tell lies about a king who comes from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejects' leaves GEMAN once the lie is gone; 'about' wraps that round the royal letter.
explanation.definitionFit: German is a specific example of foreign, being from one particular other country; the clue uses the loose sense.

clue.text: Bound along, finding sweet reduced by one penny

indicators.note: the sweet is made shorter by taking away the letters for one and penny

parts.note: a lollipop is a sweet on a stick
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone bounds along after finding a sweet marked down by a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced by' removes I and P from LOLLIPOP, leaving LOLLOP.
explanation.definitionFit: To lollop is to move along in clumsy bounding leaps, as a rabbit or a big dog does, so a verb matching the verb phrase.

clue.text: Plant in holiday area, reportedly ring-shaped

parts.note: a holiday camp is a resort area for holidaymakers

indicators.note: signals that the next part is a word as heard spoken, not as written

parts.note: annular means shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A gardener reports a plant in a holiday resort growing in a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a non-rhotic British accent, ANNULAR sounds like ANULA.
explanation.definitionFit: The campanula, or bellflower, is a genus of flowering garden plants.

clue.text: Posh fellow never meeting in centre, having no peers

parts.note: U means upper-class, the standard crossword label for posh

indicators.note: the phrase for lines that never meet goes into the middle of the posh fellow

parts.note: Ned is a familiar man's name, so any fellow
parallel lines run alongside each other and never meet

explanation.surface: A posh man never turns up to meetings in the town centre and has no equals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in centre' puts PARALLEL into the middle of UNED: UN-PARALLEL-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unparalleled means without equal, and having no peers says the same thing: nobody matches it.

clue.text: Crook flooding Nag's Head with inferior wine

indicators.note: the inferior wine pours round and engulfs the letter, so it contains it

parts.note: bad means of poor or inferior quality

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A crook swamps the Nag's Head pub with cheap plonk.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nag's Head looks like a pub name, but it means N, first letter of 'Nag's'. 'flooding' puts BAD + IT round that N. IT is the old abbreviation for Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber or outlaw, so one kind of crook.

clue.text: Accept a point gone into by party

indicators.note: the point has the party letter entering it

parts.note: a dot is a small point
P is the abbreviation for party, as in a political party

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a point after a political party takes it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone into by' means P goes inside DOT, giving DOPT, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To adopt an idea or proposal is to take it up and accept it as your own.

clue.text: Authority to carry out flunkey

parts.note: to do a task is to carry it out
a minion is a servile underling or flunkey

explanation.surface: Someone with authority makes a lackey do their bidding.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion means rule or sovereign power, which is authority over a territory or people.

clue.text: City gent going about in eastern headdress

indicators.note: the man's name goes round the word for a city

parts.note: Ted is a familiar man's name, so a gent
urban means belonging to a city

explanation.surface: A City businessman goes about in a turban from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City gent' reads as one figure, a London businessman in a bowler hat, but the two words do separate jobs, and 'going about' is the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbaned means wearing a turban, the wound cloth headwear of South Asia and the Middle East, a past-participle adjective like the phrase.

clue.text: Motoring pioneer conceals shock, given fishy concoctions

indicators.note: the pioneer's name hides the hair word inside it

parts.note: Charles Rolls co-founded Rolls-Royce in the early days of the motor car
a shock or mop of hair is a thick untidy mass of it

explanation.surface: An early motorist hides his surprise when served up fish dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks like a fright, but it means a mass of hair; 'conceals' is the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollmops are fillets of pickled herring rolled round a filling, a concocted fish dish.

clue.text: One-time procedure concerning retiring

parts.note: a form is a set procedure, as in the correct form

indicators.note: something retiring withdraws, so the word for concerning is read backwards

parts.note: re means concerning or about

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned procedure for people heading into retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns the two letters round to give ER at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Former means previous or erstwhile, which is what one-time means before a noun.

clue.text: With skill, academic had it nicely pre- CENT pared

annotationWithheld.clue: With skill, academic had it nicely pre- CENT pared

clue.text: Possibly a deeper-sounding greeting in Hawaii

indicators.note: signals that the words before it are to be heard spoken

parts.note: deeper means lower, so the phrase becomes a lower

explanation.surface: A Hawaiian greeting delivered in a more bass voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' admits the sound match is only rough: in a non-rhotic accent 'a lower' sounds roughly like ALOHA. 'deeper-sounding' looks like a single adjective about a voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloha is the Hawaiian word used both for hello and goodbye.

clue.text: Girl enters race, one with a romantic and adventurous setting

indicators.note: the girl's name goes into the word for a race

parts.note: a run is a race on foot
Rita is a girl's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl enters a race with a romantic, adventurous partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' builds RURITAN; 'with' is only a link before the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the made-up Central European kingdom of Anthony Hope's novel The Prisoner of Zenda, now the byword for a swashbuckling romantic setting.

clue.text: Influence a secure person and act unscrupulously

parts.note: pull means influence, as in having pull with someone
fast means firmly fixed or secure, as in hold fast
one means a person, as in one should

explanation.surface: Someone uses influence to secure a person and then behaves without scruples.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull a fast one is the idiom for playing a sly trick on someone, acting dishonestly.

clue.text: Papers in Oxford exam upset Check tod Trelawney's office

annotationWithheld.clue: Papers in Oxford exam upset Check tod Trelawney's office

clue.text: Underwear giving rise to audible giggles

indicators.note: signals that the word for giggles is to be heard spoken, not seen

parts.note: to nicker is to snigger or laugh quietly, so nickers are giggles

explanation.surface: Underwear that sets people off giggling.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicker, a dialect word for a snigger, sounds just like the garment because the K is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are women's pants, the British word for an undergarment.

clue.text: Short cut to Procne's transformation?

indicators.note: a transformation changes a thing's form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Procne, a figure of Greek myth, taken as written

explanation.surface: In Greek myth Procne was turned into a swallow; the clue jokes about that change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short cut' looks like a quicker route, but it is a short haircut. The joke works because Procne was turned into a bird in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eton crop is a short, slicked-down women's haircut that was fashionable in the 1920s.

clue.text: Be completely baffled, unlike the solver

definitions.meaning: to have no idea at all what is going on
a crossword solver literally has a hint in front of them, so lacking one is the opposite

explanation.surface: A self-referential joke about the person doing the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to know nothing at all, and taken literally it describes a solver with no hint.

clue.text: Champion going to city where cargo is kept

parts.note: in British usage you go up to London or a university city
a ship's hold is the space below deck where cargo is kept

explanation.surface: A champion heads into the city, where the goods are stored.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go 'up' to London or to a university city, whatever the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause is to support or defend it, which is what uphold means; both are verbs.

clue.text: Inventor's absence of pretentiousness when climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: side means a pretentious, superior air, so having none is no side

explanation.surface: An inventor stays modest as they climb in the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' is old British slang for putting on airs. 'when climbing' turns NO SIDE upwards to read EDISON.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American who developed the phonograph and a practical electric light bulb.

clue.text: Small carnivore potentially making decent pie

indicators.note: the letters could become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something that might turn up in a decent pie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' rearranges DECENT PIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A centipede is a small many-legged creature that hunts and eats insects, so a meat-eater.

clue.text: Byzantine ruler in dire need

indicators.note: the ruler's name is held within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: An Eastern emperor finds themselves in desperate straits.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene of Athens ruled the Byzantine Empire in her own right at the end of the eighth century.

clue.text: Fast quietly observed in middle of attack

indicators.note: the quiet letter goes into the centre of the attack word

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
p, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Someone quickly and quietly watched from the heart of an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observed' only joins the pieces: P is put in RAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid means fast or swift, both adjectives describing speed.

clue.text: Made English composer duke

parts.note: Thomas Arne was the eighteenth-century English composer of Rule, Britannia

explanation.surface: An English composer was made a duke.
explanation.definitionFit: To have earned money is to have made it; both are past forms meaning gained by work.

clue.text: Painstaking boss promises to pay

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a round knob sticking out of a surface
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A careful boss hands out promises to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' looks like an employer, but it is a raised knob, a STUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Studious can mean diligent and careful, which is what painstaking describes.

clue.text: Firm keeping record with introduction to this work

indicators.note: the firm word holds the record inside it

parts.note: set means firm or solid, as jelly sets
an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A company keeps a record that opens its new work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a company but means solid; 'keeping' is the containment and 'introduction to' gives the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A septet is a piece of music written for seven players, so a musical work.

clue.text: Wow! Fielder saves run — he's a keen backer-up

indicators.note: the exclamation and fielder hold the run letter between them

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise, like wow
mid-on is a cricket fielding position near the bowler on the leg side
R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder saves a run, and a supporter cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-on is a cricket fielding position. 'saves' holds the run letter between the exclamation and the fielder.
explanation.definitionFit: A myrmidon is a loyal follower who carries out orders without question, after Achilles's soldiers in Homer.
